info.bio: Banda oriunda de la ciudad de Toronto, Canada, nacida en 1977, dentro del naciente movimiento punk/new wave/art pop; con una ecléctica mezcla de influencias ( formas libres del jazz, musica experimental, el sonido Motown, Roxy Music y The Beatles), rapidamente se hicieron un nombre dentro del circuito universitario local. Su primer album "Metro Music" fue registrado en Inglaterra en 1979, obteniendo un significativo exito con el tema "Echo Beach"

scenes.name: Música de baile para punks
scenes.author: Piero Scaruffi
scenes.desc: La disco y el punk florecen a la vez y acaban fusionándose, pese a representar valores casi opuestos. Blondie define la fusión de hedonismo disco y estética punk; Madonna es el híbrido definitivo y redefine la balada de rhythm'n'blues para la era de los ritmos electrónicos. Las mujeres llevan la actitud punk a las discotecas. Talking Heads asimilan el funk en la canción new wave y, con Eno, llegan a la fusión de futurismo y primitivismo de Remain In Light; Byrne y Eno firman My Life In The Bush Of Ghosts. ESG, Liquid Liquid, Defunkt, Bush Tetras, los Contortions de James Chance (Albert Ayler + Beefheart + James Brown), la Love Of Life Orchestra de Peter Gordon, Suburbs, Was Not Was, Wall Of Voodoo.

mentions.author: Piero Scaruffi
mentions.text: …stylish sonic puzzles that offered an effervescent re-interpretation of black dance music in a high-tech white (and hard-rock) context. In Canada, Martha & The Muffins bridged B52's, the Canterbury sound and pop-jazz on Metro Music (1979). 134

podcast.title: Long-Term Unmarried Relationship (Since 1981)
podcast.body: Martha Johnson and founding member Tim Gain of Martha and the muffins have been together since 1981. Despite common assumptions, they have not married. "Martha Johnson and founding member Tim Gain together since 1981 and despite what you may have read, not married."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Artwork Designer
podcast.body: Peter Saville, chief art design guy at Factory Records, did design work for Martha and the Muffins. "He did everything from gig posters to album design for Joy Division New Order, Roxas music, Swade, pulp, Martha Nemuffins, and Noam D."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Collaboration with Daniel Lanois
podcast.body: After learning from Brian Eno, Daniel Lanois applied his new recording techniques to sessions with bands like Martha and the Muffins. "Landwom learned a lot about recording music which he then applied to sessions with bands like Martha and the Muffins and the Parachute Club."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Daniel Lanois Production
podcast.body: Daniel Lanois, brother of former bassist Jostelyn Lanois, also contributed to the band's music by serving as a producer for some of their recordings. "Brother Daniel also produced music for Martha and the muffins."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Grant Avenue Studios Recording Artists
podcast.body: Martha and the Muffins recorded material at Grant Avenue Studios around 1983-84, overlapping with David Botrell's early assistantship. "Martha and the Muffins in the parachute club and Luba. Those records were going on while I was there."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Ongoing Band Activity
podcast.body: The band technically still exists and is currently managed by original members Martha Johnson and Mark Gane. "And technically the band still exists, run by Martha Johnson and Mark Gain."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Origin at Ontario College of Art and Design
podcast.body: The group originated at the Ontario College of Art and Design, where Martha Ladly, an early member, later became a professor. "Ontario College of Art and Design, which is where Martha and the muffins began, we back when."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Collaboration with Daniel Lanois
xref.body: Impressed by Daniel Lanois's production of a "Time Twins" track, Brian Eno booked studio time with Lanois at Grand Avenue to work on his early ambient records, thereby mentoring Lanois in recording music. "Eno was so impressed that he booked time with Dan at Grand Avenue to work on some of his early ambient records and over the next couple of years Landwom learned a lot about recording music which he then applied to sessions with bands like Martha and the Muffins and the Parachute Club."

xref.title: Mentorship by Brian Eno
xref.body: Brian Eno, impressed by a track Lanois produced for Time Twins, booked studio time with Lanois at Grand Avenue. Over several years, Lanois gained extensive knowledge about recording music while working on Eno's early ambient records. "Eno was so impressed that he booked time with Dan at Grand Avenue to work on some of his early ambient records and over the next couple of years Landwom learned a lot about recording music which he then applied to sessions with bands like Martha and the Muffins and the Parachute Club."

xref.title: Post-Muffins Career in UK
xref.body: After leaving Martha and the Muffins, Martha Ladly moved to the UK, where she pursued recording, joined Robert Palmer's band, and collaborated with Elbamar designer Peter Saville, known for his work with Factory Records bands like Joy Division and New Order. "As she quit, she moved to the UK, did some recording, joined up with Robert Palmer's band, did work with Elba Martin designer Peter Savil, the guy who did so much for factory records bands like Joy Division and New Order."
